Every candidate a build produces is measured, and the measurement is what
the judge scores and the campaign optimises. The evaluator is therefore the
one thing a campaign must never be allowed to improve. This page is the
contract an evaluator meets and the three states one can be in.

## The contract

An evaluator is a command the campaign runs from the workspace root. A good
one:

- runs in one command: `python kapso_evaluation/evaluate.py`, with the
  candidate's own entry point called inside it;
- prints the metric as its last line, `name: value`, such as `auc: 0.8412`,
  and writes `kapso_evaluation/result.json` with `evaluation_script_path`,
  `evaluation_output` and `score`;
- exits non-zero with a printed reason on a malformed submission, so a
  broken candidate is a clear failure, not a low score;
- is deterministic given the candidate, so repeats agree and the noise you
  care about is the data's, which you can state (a bootstrap standard
  error beside the baseline);
- has a `--fast` mode for smoke checks, marked not comparable with a full
  score;
- finishes well under a minute per cycle where the task allows, so a
  build's budget goes to experiments, not to measuring them.

The [churn example](/docs/first-build) ships one that meets every line.

## Provided: yours, protected

Pass the directory with `--evaluation` (Python: `evaluation=`). It is copied
to `kapso_evaluation/` in the workspace, committed as the baseline and
fingerprinted, file by file. A candidate that modifies, deletes, replaces or
extends it is rejected: its score is cleared, the judge never sees it, and
it is never chosen as a parent or delivered. The count of such candidates is
`solution.rejected_candidates`. New runtime artifacts (`result.json`, logs,
predictions) are allowed; new evaluator source is not. The mechanics are
on [Evaluation integrity](/docs/evolve/evaluation-integrity).

Data goes the same way: `--data` (Python: `data=`) is copied to
`kapso_datasets/`. Keep hold-out labels out of both directories; the
evaluator reaches them where you put them, and the rules in the brief say
no candidate may.

## Proposed: built from the brief

With no `--evaluation`, the campaign's first node builds the evaluator in
`kapso_evaluation/` from the brief's `Measured by` line: the data, the
split, the seed, the metric and how it is printed. The judge then reads
every candidate's evaluation against the brief, and a candidate that
weakens the protocol is scored as what it is. Write the protocol
precisely; the [fraud example](https://github.com/Leeroo-AI/kapso/tree/main/examples/fraud-no-evaluator)
shows one.

What the shipped config does not do yet is register that evaluator and
protect it file by file the way a provided one is protected. That is the
evaluation maintainer's job, and the maintainer runs only when the
config's `evaluation_maintainer` block is set (the RelBench benchmark
config sets one; `GENERIC` and `MINIMAL` do not). The config package of
the redesign decides the default.

## Versioned: the registry

When the evaluation maintainer runs, every evaluator the campaign uses is
a version in `.kapso/evaluation_registry.json`, with its provenance:
`provided`, `maintainer_built` (proposed from the brief) or `derived_fast`
(a fast mode derived from a full one). A score never crosses a version
boundary. The version the delivered candidate was measured under is
`solution.evaluator`:

```python
solution.evaluator             # EvaluatorRef(version=1, evaluator_id="…", provenance="provided")
solution.evaluator is None     # no maintainer ran, so nothing was registered
```

Without the maintainer, `solution.evaluator` is `None` for a provided
evaluator too; the provided evaluator is still protected by the integrity
check above.

## Your own evaluator in Python

A caller-owned evaluator can also run once per finalized candidate, in an
isolated worktree, with its metrics kept out of the search loop:
`build(..., iteration_evaluator=callback)`. The metrics of the delivered
candidate are `solution.callback_metrics`. See
[External evaluation](/docs/evolve/external-evaluation) for the callback's
contract and failure policy.
